Graduate Students and Researchers: Two PhD students who are pursuing their graduate studies have their theses related to this project involving experimental setup development, conducting experiments, data analysis as well as theoretical modeling and simulation. In addition, we have had several undergraduate students helping with the project and a post-doctoral researcher working on the project. Conclusions An experimental setup capable of monitoring and capturing instantaneous drying characteristics with high resolutions was developed to accurately study the alternating conductive and convective drying of paper and board. This provided important fundamental insights on the drying process and meaningful heat and mass transfer correlations that can be used for design, modeling and simulation. Experimental investigation of the integration of RF and US energies at varying drying times and sheet moisture conditions during alternating conduction and convection drying (i.e. duplicating commercial multi-cylinder drying) has also been evaluated. Integrating RF drying is indeed an effective method for paper drying applications with greater improvements in drying rates and energy intensities at higher moisture contents. RF drying is especially effective at higher basis weights, as in packaging grades, which are, in general, more difficult to dry using the current commercial technologies. US applications in the pockets (along with convection) after conduction on the cylinders are more favorable resulting in reasonable improvements in drying rate and energy intensity for all basis weights studied. This suggests adding US in the pockets with pocket ventilation systems might be the desired approach. With optimal integration of RFUS technology we were able to alter the drying rate profile and improve the overall drying performance. Results clearly showed that with optimum integration of RFUS at various locations/sheet moisture contents on the paper machine, the desired target improvements in drying rate and drying time achieving the project goals. A paper drying transport model considering the mass, energy and momentum transport with associated governing equations, initial and boundary conditions has been developed and solved using multi-physics, computational simulation approaches. With appropriate model parameters including liquid permeability, gas permeability, diffusivity, heat and mass transfer coefficients the simulation results compared reasonably well with commercial machine data as well as with 59 DE-EE0009395 experimental data. Based on experimental data and modeling and simulation results, we have shown that with optimal integration of the RFUS, we can achieve necessary improvements in drying rates compared to the base case conduction and convection, reaching the minimum and stretch target improvements in overall drying rates. The TEA and LCA of implementing RFUS technology in commercial paper production shows high energy savings, enhanced drying and production rates, and a reduced carbon footprint. These outcomes are due to the application of two scenarios: replacing the steam cylinders (conduction) with RF technology and implementing US in the pockets to enhance convection after the cylinder conduction.
